title: dedicated-autoscaler-priority-routing-burst-util-reporting-enhancement
author: Alex Chen
release_notes: Added priority-based burst controls to Dedicated autoscaler and expanded fleet utilization reporting to include burst consumption and per-priority latency buckets. Config opt-in and no breaking API changes.
body: Context: Customers using Dedicated fleets requested clearer guarantees around short-term burst capacity and visibility by customer priority. This PR implements a priority-aware burst tokenbucket, exposes new time-series metrics for burst consumption and queueing across priority tiers, and wires reporting into the fleet dashboards. Summary of changes: 1) Autoscaler: introduce 'priority_burst' policy that assigns per-priority token buckets with configurable refill and window parameters; 2) Runtime: apply priority routing in scheduler so high-priority requests can draw from reserved burst tokens; 3) Metrics: emit redwood.dedicated.burst_consumed, redwood.dedicated.burst_available, and redwood.dedicated.priority_latency_buckets (p0-p3) with consistent labels (fleet_id, priority); 4) API/Config: add fleet autoscale schema fields (priority_burst.enabled, priority_burst.p0_reserve_pct, refill_rate_ms, window_ms); 5) UI: dashboard panels for burst utilization and per-priority latency heatmaps; 6) Tests: unit + integration harness covering tokenbucket edgecases and e2e in perf-canary. Motivation: previously bursts were globally allocated causing noisy neighbors and limited visibility; this adds an isolation knob and observability to allow teams to set SLOs per customer tier. Design notes: tokenbucket smoothing borrowed from existing autoscaler smoothing code with a priority reservation layer; fallbacks added so if priority buckets are exhausted, lower-priority requests either queue (if queueing enabled) or are routed to fallback model variants. Backwards compatibility: default for priority_burst.enabled=false so no change to existing fleets unless explicitly enabled. Rollout plan: staged rollout — feature gated behind config flag; apply to canary fleet, monitor new metrics for 48h, enable for staging fleets, then gradual 25% increments by fleet. Downgrade path: disable priority_burst flag and autoscaler reverts to legacy behavior. Checklist: - [x] Design doc linked (ENG-7821) - [x] Unit tests - [x] Integration tests in perf-canary - [x] Dashboard panels added - [x] Docs update draft in redwood-docs - [x] Backwards-compatible default behavior - [x] Feature gated for staged rollout Known limitations: tokenbucket parameters require tuning per workload; long-running bursts still consume base capacity and could affect throughput guarantees if misconfigured. Related: ENG-7821, ENG-7950, SUP-321.
commit_summary: squash! autoscaler: add priority_burst policy; runtime: priority tokenbucket enforcement; metrics: emit burst_consumed/available and priority_latency_buckets; console: add burst panels; tests: unit/integration/perf-canary
review_comments: Priya Gupta: Please add an e2e that covers priority exhaustion fallback behavior — we need a test that verifies routing to fallback model variants under high contention.
Alex Chen: Added perf-canary e2e and a unit that simulates exhaustion; test included in this PR (see tests/perf).
Marcus Lee: Can we make the metric labels consistent with existing fleet labels (region, env)? Looks good otherwise; one nit on renaming p0->priority_0 for clarity.
Dana Rivera: Verified dashboard panels in staging; metrics are coming through and help identify burst hot windows. Approving once minor naming nit is addressed.
author_responses: Alex Chen: Renamed metric labels to include region and env, and changed bucket names to priority_0..priority_3; updated tests accordingly.
notes: Hotfix follow-up planned: tweak default p0_reserve_pct from 10 to 15 based on canary telemetry (separate PR).
